system.summary: Graphic substitution alphabet with special doubled-letter signs and nulls; close to, but not identical with, Nevers collection no. 2 of 1584.

diacritics.note: Related key uses marked or compound signs for doubled consonants.

system.sibling_key: Nevers collection no. 2, BnF fr. 3995 f. 16 (1584); similar but not exact. Tomokiyo notes F=e and 9=q on the 1574 leaves, with x, y, z in clear.
system.notes: The exact 1574 table was not reconstructed. The target supplies stronger evidence than the sibling: an interlinear decipherment on f. 15 and a parallel clear copy on f. 21.

prior_solution.where: The manuscript itself preserves a contemporary interlinear decipherment on f. 15, a clear ending on f. 16r, and a complete clear copy under the cipher flap on f. 21; Tomokiyo described the system but published no reading.

conditions.human_role: The human selected the target and requested a solve/read followed by a write-up. No target-specific transcription or cryptanalytic intervention.

solution.what: Mapped manuscript folios to Gallica openings and fetched full-resolution images of ff. 15 and 21 and the neighbouring keys.
Found and transcribed the complete clear Italian fair copy beneath Birago's cipher flap at f. 21.
Identified the small writing between the cipher lines of f. 15 as a contemporary word-by-word decipherment, not random pen trials.
Fetched Nevers no. 2 of 1584 from BnF fr. 3995 f. 16 and confirmed that it is only a sibling key, not the exact target alphabet.
Checked a superficially similar Henri III appeal printed by Lavisse and rejected it as a crib because it predates this letter and has a different sender.
Read the opening on f. 15 and the clear ending on f. 16r; continuous transcription of the cipher leaves remained blocked by the overwritten minute hand.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): decryptions f15_reading.md (opening, address and clear ending only) and f21_transcription.md (the clear fair copy); no sign-level transcription of either cipher exists in the folder

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): f21_transcription.md reads as continuous Italian (reviewed A); f15_reading.md gives only the opening of the gloss, the address and the clear closing, so f. 15 is relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.4 -> about 0.3 (estimated).

Re-read of f. 15 under REREAD_BRIEF (batch mix1): the interlinear gloss transcribed line by line on the Gallica native images (f15_gloss.md), the cipher signs transcribed (f15_signs.tsv, 70 lines; f. 16r lines 1-19 found to continue the cipher) and decoded with an alphabet rebuilt from gloss-sign alignment (f15_key.md). Gloss and decode agree word for word on f. 15r and f. 16r; f. 15v ll. 2-5 illegible. f. 15 relabelled read (f15_reading.md, f15_en.md, f15_reread_log.md).
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 2 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent check (verify_dudout_20261114.py, f15_key.md and f15_signs.tsv only): the reading enciphered back with the key agrees with the transcribed signs on 942 of 978 (f. 15r), 637 of 781 (f. 15v) and 587 of 620 (f. 16r cipher) collapsed signs. The ~50 one- or two-letter differences on 15r/16r are mostly letters the transcription omits, plus two regular usages f15_key.md does not list: 'gouvernement' is written 0 8 2 ... (2 = n for u) in all five occurrences, and the d-sign b stands for u/v three times (15r ll. 2, 8, 26); 15r ll. 2 and 8 checked on the Gallica image (f17): as transcribed. f. 15v ll. 2-5 re-read at full size: nothing new. v10_relabel.measure 0.941 = recorded.

Project check of PR #572 (Brice Dudout): his script re-run (942/978, 637/781, 587/620 collapsed signs agree with the reading enciphered back). The two usages checked in f15_signs.tsv: 0 8 2 for gou- in the five occurrences of gouvernement (15r ll. 8, 10, 15; 15v l. 23; 16r l. 12) and b for u/v at 15r ll. 2, 8, 26; added to f15_key.md under 'Homophones and traps' as usages, not table values. v10_relabel.measure 0.941 as recorded; read in part stands. Gallica f17 fetched; ll. 2 and 8 not read again here.

outcome.method_basis: f. 21 was read from the complete contemporary clear copy under Birago's cipher flap. f. 15 (with its continuation on f. 16r) was read from its contemporary interlinear decipherment, checked against a mechanical decode with the alphabet rebuilt from gloss-sign alignment (close to, but not, the 1584 Nevers no. 2 alphabet: e=F, q and s=9, d=b-shape, m=+, t=4, a doubling sign, name signs for Roy, Royne mere, Royne).
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, re-read (batch mix1): both documents now read. Tokens: f. 21 clear copy 271 words, all read; f. 15-16 cipher 626 tokens in f15_reading.md (70 cipher lines; the 84 words of the clear closing excluded), of which 54 are [...] holes (50 on f. 15v). (271 + 572) / (271 + 626) = 0.94. Withdrawn: 0.3 (page-weighted estimate of the reading audit, before f. 15 was read).
outcome.notes: Both leaves preserve their own reading aids: f. 21 a clear copy under the flap, f. 15 an interlinear decipherment, used with a rebuilt alphabet. f. 15v ll. 2-5 stay illegible on the best image.

texts.label: Henriette de Clèves to the duke of Nevers, Lyon, 16 Sept [1574], ff. 15-16
texts.summary: The duchess tells her husband that Pignerol and Savillan have been handed to the Duke of Savoy, to the contentment of the King and the Queen Mother, so that Nevers is left without his government; her exchange with the Queen Mother (who first approves warning him, then says he does not lose his government) and her tears; a report to the King that Nevers had written of a league of four or five near the King; promises of the next vacant government (Picardy, Languedoc); his friends say he would harm himself by keeping the reduced government. Cipher continues on f. 16r (19 lines), then a clear closing: it is midnight, she would rather be in paradise.

reading_review.note: f15_reading.md: the contemporary interlinear gloss (f15_gloss.md) and a mechanical decode of the cipher signs (f15_signs.tsv, alphabet f15_key.md rebuilt from gloss-sign alignment) agree word for word on f. 15r and f. 16r; 70 cipher lines. f. 15r and the f. 16r cipher read as continuous French (4 holes in 402 tokens); f. 15v ll. 2-5 are overwritten and their gloss faded (illegible), with a dozen single groups open further down, 50 holes in 224 tokens. _check_reading on the reading body: 46 of 57 sentences clean (0.81). Verified word by word 22 Oct 2026 (verify2_nevers_align.py: signs decoded with f15_key.md, gloss words aligned): 0 words bracketed beyond those already marked, 3 replaced (f. 15v l. 16 "desquoy elle m'a dict [...] tesmoigner" -> "desquoy mesme [?pouvoit] tesmoigner": signs +F9+F (9886..74, gloss "mesme ... [?pouvoit]"); 0.807 clean on the body (unchanged).

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 94.1% of the words of f15_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: Renato Birago to the duke of Nevers, Lyon, 28 Sept 1574, f. 21

reading_review.note: f21_transcription.md: the contemporary clear fair copy under the cipher flap, transcribed as continuous Italian; every sentence reads, one doubtful word (saluato suo).

texts.summary: Birago had expected Nevers in Lyon for St Michael's day; the bearer's business comes at the worst moment, as the affairs of the kingdom make anything else more urgent; Birago will speak of Piedmont by mouth; Their Majesties are well disposed to give Nevers a government and whatever else he deserves. The decryption is the clear fair copy on the same recto; the cipher flap itself was not transcribed sign by sign.
